name: Vitruvian Classicism
summary: Architecture organised around firmitas (firmness), utilitas (commodity), venustas (delight). Reanimated through Renaissance treatises (Alberti, Palladio).

name: Garden City
summary: Howard's diagrammatic third magnet — combining country and city. Decentralised, polycentric settlements of ~30,000 people surrounded by greenbelts.

name: Bauhaus
summary: Gropius's school unifying art, craft, and industrial production. Foundational to the International Style.

name: Modernism
summary: Form follows function; ornament is crime. Mass-produced housing, structural rationality, the free plan.

name: CIAM
summary: Congrès Internationaux d'Architecture Moderne (1928-1959). Athens Charter (1933) prescribed functional zoning of the city.

name: Postmodernism
summary: Reaction to modernist purism. Venturi's Complexity and Contradiction (1966), Learning from Las Vegas (1972). Symbol, history, irony.

name: Critical Regionalism
summary: Frampton's Towards a Critical Regionalism (1983) — architecture grounded in place, climate, light, and material while resisting kitsch.
sources: Towards a Critical Regionalism, K. Frampton, 1983

name: New Urbanism
summary: Charter of the New Urbanism (1996). Walkable, mixed-use neighbourhoods organised around the transect from rural to urban core.

name: Transit-Oriented Development
summary: Calthorpe's The Next American Metropolis (1993). Compact mixed-use development within walking distance of high-quality transit.
sources: The Next American Metropolis, P. Calthorpe, 1993

name: Complete Streets
summary: Streets designed for all users — pedestrians, cyclists, transit, motorists. National Complete Streets Coalition (US, 2005).

name: Biophilic Urbanism
summary: Beatley (2010) — cities that connect residents to nature through canopy, green infrastructure, biodiversity, and direct contact with living systems.

name: Parametricism
summary: Schumacher's Parametricism manifesto (2008) — architecture as a continuous variation of differentiated systems, parametric modelling as primary medium.

name: 15-Minute City
summary: Moreno's framework: every essential daily need accessible within 15 minutes by foot or bike. Implemented in Paris under Mayor Hidalgo.
